clue.text: Strongly anger unionists, being enthusiastic

parts.note: to fire someone is to inflame them, rouse them to strong feeling
the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: Someone enraging Ulster unionists and getting excited about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP (Democratic Unionist Party) is a Northern Ireland political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fired up is an idiom for being keen and full of zeal.

clue.text: Iron rod upon a hat

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: read as up on, it sends the word up the column, backwards in a down clue

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Pressing an iron bar down onto a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upon' acts as 'up on': in a down answer the rod is written upwards, giving DOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown.

clue.text: Brief script, yet evenly read

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters of each word are taken: second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A short text that should still be spoken smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: Brief gives RE, script gives CIT, yet gives E, each word counted on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to say aloud from memory or from a page.

clue.text: First in cold blast to become agitated

indicators.note: the ordinal goes inside the chilly gust

parts.note: a draught is a cold current of air
1st, written with I as the figure one

explanation.surface: Being hit first by an icy wind leaves one upset.
explanation.walkthrough: IST imitates 1ST, the ordinal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraught means deeply upset and overwrought, beside oneself with worry.

clue.text: What could make Cupid easily embarrassed

indicators.note: the letters of the god's name could be made into another word by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Wondering what would make the god of love blush readily.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudic is a rare word for modest or bashful, from Latin pudor, shame.

clue.text: Not quite have time to cover puzzles, essentially reversing instruction

indicators.note: the whole assembly is then read backwards
the shortened pair goes around, covering, the middle letter of puzzles
each of the two words loses its final letter, so neither is quite complete

parts.note: the two words written together, each to be shortened

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Someone short of time to work on puzzles, with a note about reversing as a step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims HAVE and TIME to HAV and TIM; 'to cover' puts Z, the centre of puzzles, between them: HAVZTIM; 'reversing' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitzvah is a commandment of Jewish law, a religious precept or directive.

clue.text: In a kind of miracle, they say you are fickle

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the rearranged word
a kind of means a version of, so these letters are rearranged
they say means the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: said aloud the two words sound like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: A changeable person, called a sort of wonder by others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' signals text-speak spelling of 'you are' as two letters; 'In' sets them inside the rearranged miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercurial means volatile and changeable, like the quick-moving god Mercury.

clue.text: One left rusticated arrangement of flowers in grief

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the remaining letters in a new order
left means gone away, so the letter departs from the word

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single floral display, left out in the country, in a time of mourning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' are things that flow: the glands' channels carry tears when we cry. 'left' removes I from rusticated; 'arrangement' shuffles RUSTCATED.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducts draining the eyes are the channels through which tears pour when someone weeps.

clue.text: May be even true of sex

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form another word, so they are rearranged

parts.note: real and true both mean genuine

explanation.surface: A cautious claim that equality might hold between the sexes.
explanation.definitionFit: Venereal means relating to sexual desire or intercourse, from Venus.

clue.text: Write down curse for Spooner's nags

indicators.note: Spooner's means swapping the opening sounds of two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a pen is what you write with, and to pen is to write
a hex is a spell or curse

explanation.surface: Instructions to note a jinx on some old horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nags' looks like horses but is the verb. Swapping the first sounds of PEN HEX gives a phrase heard as hen pecks.
explanation.definitionFit: To henpeck is to nag or domineer over someone, typically a spouse.

clue.text: See 6
Exceptional grant and a fourth armed man?

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remarkable funding award, plus a quarter share, seemingly for a man with weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: The Three Musketeers were joined by a fourth swordsman, the hero of Dumas's novel; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumas's hero joins Athos, Porthos and Aramis as the fourth musketeer, a swordsman carrying arms.

clue.text: Humanitarian organisation's driver possibly going round in circles

parts.note: rotary describes motion turning about an axis
a driver is one kind of golf club

explanation.surface: A charity's chauffeur, perhaps lost and circling endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' points to a motorist but is the golf club, and 'going round in circles' describes it as rotary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rotary movement is an international service body of local branches doing charitable work.

clue.text: Fortitude may be needed in readiness for real snow and ice

definitions.text: may be needed in readiness for real snow and ice
definitions.meaning: read literally, actual ... is what is spread on roads before genuine wintry weather

explanation.surface: Bravery is needed when preparing for a proper winter freeze.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: real (true) grit, the gravel spread on icy roads, as British councils do in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means courage and toughness, made famous by the Western film of that title.

clue.text: Unattended vehicle's broken into in Paris: a damaged Ford

indicators.note: the vehicle has broken into the French word, landing inside it

parts.note: une is the feminine French for a
a car is a vehicle; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: An abandoned car broken into in Paris, a wrecked Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: French 'a' here is the feminine form, not the masculine one a solver may try first; 'broken into' means the vehicle goes inside it, and 'damaged' scrambles Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left uncared-for is neglected, with nobody looking after it.

clue.text: Is Monet misrepresented in tiny but fundamental matter?

definitions.text: Is Monet misrepresented in tiny but fundamental matter?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are set inside the particle's name

parts.note: a quark is an elementary particle of matter

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether the painter Monet is wrongly portrayed in some small yet basic point.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue's own closing punctuation mark: the whole clue both builds the answer and ends with what it names.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation ending the clue is exactly the symbol named, so the clue defines itself by its final character.

clue.text: From the time of Rome, it took years to start with honesty

parts.note: since means from the time of
R is the abbreviation for Rome, as on Italian car plates

indicators.note: to start with means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A historical remark that Rome took ages to build, followed by a tribute to truthfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincerity is the quality of being genuine and truthful, free from deceit.

clue.text: Snob houses closed, only half occupied

indicators.note: only the back half of each word is kept

explanation.surface: A snob's houses are shut, with only half of them lived in.
explanation.walkthrough: The second halves are OB, SES and SED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be obsessed is to have the mind preoccupied by one thing.

clue.text: Weapon of racism (lost without it)

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the scrambled letters surround the two-letter word
lost suggests the letters have gone astray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instrument of bigotry, with the parenthetical aside that it lacks something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: the anagram SCIMAR goes around IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved sword associated with the Middle East.

clue.text: Merrymaking composer pens the ultimate in music, rejecting secure articles

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the composer's name holds the next letter

parts.note: J S Bach, the composer

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter
rejecting means throwing back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: to nail something down is to secure it
AN and A are both indefinite articles

explanation.surface: A jolly composer writes with a flourish, turning down guaranteed items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' reverses NAIL + AN + A to give ANALIAN, after BACCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Bacchus, god of wine, the word describes drunken revelry and riotous celebration.

clue.text: Long live the Emperor of Zanzibar, unclothed and dancing

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters are rearranged
unclothed means stripped of its outer layers, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cheer for the ruler of Zanzibar, naked and dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping Zanzibar gives ANZIBA, which 'dancing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Banzai is a Japanese cheer wishing the emperor ten thousand years of life.

clue.text: Part of Venezuela due for uprising, like most of Europe once

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the letters from bottom to top
part of means the letters are a run within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A region of Venezuela set to revolt, as much of Europe did historically.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval Europe was largely organised under the system of lords, vassals and fiefs.

clue.text: Redeem myself, partly to get an award

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer hoping to make amends by winning a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the American television industry's prize, so the definition names a trophy to be won.

clue.text: Consider purposeful shop reprimand

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
to berate is to scold

explanation.surface: Think about a determined telling-off for a store.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions sit together at the start: the verb meaning to ponder, and the adjective meaning intentional.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to weigh up carefully; as an adjective it means done on purpose, intentional.

clue.text: Brought up breakfast cereal, bypassing the beginning of stomach and small intestine

indicators.note: bypassing means leaving out, so the letter is dropped
brought up in a down clue means written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: muesli is a breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and fruit

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Vomiting breakfast, sparing the stomach but passing through the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' reverses MUESLI to ILSEUM; 'bypassing' drops its S. The definition is loose: this is the last part of the small intestine.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the final section of the small intestine, before the colon.

clue.text: See 12
Desolate nature's in evolution

indicators.note: evolution is gradual change, so these letters develop into a new order

explanation.surface: A bleak observation that the natural world is always developing.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, sombre temperament, linked astrologically to the planet Saturn.

clue.text: Bothered bit by bit, as they say

indicators.note: as they say signals that the word must be heard spoken

parts.note: something introduced in stages is phased

explanation.surface: Someone gradually troubled, so the saying goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fazed means being disconcerted or flustered.

clue.text: Parker cooked hot fish outside

definitions.note: Dorothy Parker, the American wit and writer

indicators.note: the fish's name goes outside the scrambled letters

parts.note: the dory is a sea fish (John Dory)

indicators.note: cooked means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who parks has prepared a spicy fish dish wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parker' looks like a person parking, but it is the surname of the American writer Dorothy Parker; 'cooked' makes OTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the famous New York humorist and poet whose surname is the definition.

clue.text: About marriage, when it turns belligerent

indicators.note: the two letters of the word it are flipped round in place

parts.note: marital means relating to marriage

explanation.surface: Wedlock that turns sour and combative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' acts only on the two-letter word 'it' inside the adjective, flipping those letters in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial means warlike, relating to fighting and armed forces.
